title: The Tate twist line is a rank-one lisse adic sheaf and twisting is the lisse tensor
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $X$ be a separated noetherian scheme of finite dimension on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], let $T_{E,n}=A_{E,n,X}(m)$ be the étale Tate sheaf of [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-sheaf] on the small étale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], formed with $N=\ell^n$ (which kills $A_{E,n}$). Then:

1. Reduction modulo $\varpi_E^n$ (with $u\mapsto u^\ell$ on roots of unity, and for $m<0$ through the dual) gives isomorphisms $T_{E,n+1}\otimes_{A_{E,n+1}}A_{E,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E,n}$, and each $T_{E,n}$ is étale locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $A_{E,n,X}$. Hence $\mathcal T_E=(T_{E,n})_{n\ge1}$ is a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf of rank one in the sense of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], and $\mathcal T=(E,\mathcal T_E\otimes E)$ is a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf whose fibre $\mathcal T_{\bar x}$ [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors] at every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] is a one-dimensional $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-vector space; up to canonical isomorphism $\mathcal T$ does not depend on $E$.

2. With $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], there are isomorphisms $\nu_X^{*}T_{E,n}\cong A_{E,n}(m)_X$ with the finite-level twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], compatible with the transition maps, and $\varprojlim_n\nu_X^{*}T_{E,n}\cong\mathcal O_E(m)_X$. Thus the object of $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] given by $\mathcal T$ in degree zero, namely $\mathcal O_E(m)_X$ rationalized and taken at the finite stage $E$, is the twist object $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}(m)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

3. For every $K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ the Tate twist $K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda(m)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] is naturally isomorphic to the tensor product $K\otimes^L\mathcal T$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] (the completed integral tensor product, rationalized and extended to a common finite stage); in particular, on an integral representative the uncompleted derived tensor product with the invertible line $\mathcal O_E(m)_X$ is already derived complete and agrees with the completed one.

proof.text: At finite level, the Kummer sheaf $\mu_{\ell^r,X}$ is etale locally the constant cyclic sheaf and its transition maps are the power maps. The finite Tate sheaf construction and the finite-twist line lemma therefore identify $T_{E,n}$ with the locally constant rank-one sheaf $A_{E,n}(m)$ and identify reduction along $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$ with the displayed map; for $m<0$ the same assertion follows by taking the sheaf dual of the positive twist, using the invertibility of the Tate line. The compatible locally free rank-one reductions are exactly a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf of rank one in the adic sense, and their scalar extension to a common finite stage gives a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf with one-dimensional geometric fibres. The common-stage construction is independent of the chosen finite coefficient field $E$ up to its canonical scalar-extension identifications. More explicitly, $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $e\geq1$, so $\ell^nA_{E,n}=0$. On an etale cover with a primitive $\ell^{n+1}$-st root $\zeta$, the transition sends the generator $\zeta$ to the primitive root $\zeta^\ell$, so after coefficient reduction its matrix is $1$. Tensor powers and the inverse of the dual base-change isomorphism give the same matrix for every signed twist. At a geometric point compatible bases can be chosen successively, since units of $A_{E,n}$ lift to units of $A_{E,n+1}$; their inverse limit is a basis over $\mathcal O_E$.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.5; Definition 6.8.3 and Proposition 6.8.4(1); Remark 6.8.15, together with the finite etale Kummer construction

proof.text:
For a finite etale $X$-scheme $P$, the comparison adjunction identifies $
u_X^*h_P$ with the pro-etale sheaf represented by the same $P$: maps from either object to $G$ are $G(P)$, by adjunction and Yoneda, naturally in $P$. Apply this to the finite etale roots-of-unity schemes and their power maps. The exact constant-coefficient inverse image of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] then identify the positive finite twists. For a rank-one line the pullback of its dual is its dual, since the evaluation comparison is the identity on a local basis; this gives the negative twists too. The Kummer-level independence in [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free], clause 2, and the reduction formula of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] identify these objects with $A_{E,n}(m)_X$, compatibly with coefficient reduction. For the inverse limit, use the compatible primitive-root pro-etale cover of [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free], clause 1. On its slice site the canonical maps $\mathcal O_E(m)_X	o A_{E,n}(m)_X$ are the quotient maps $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}	o(A_{E,n})_X$ in the induced tensor or dual bases. Their limit is an isomorphism by the definition of the completed coefficient sheaf. Slice restriction commutes with limits (sections on each object compute both limits), so these canonical local isomorphisms prove $\mathcal O_E(m)_X\cong\varprojlim_n
u_X^*T_{E,n}$ globally. No assertion that $
u_X^*$ commutes with infinite limits is used.

proof.text: The integral categories underlying [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] must first be compared. The scheme $X$ is noetherian and finite-dimensional with $\ell$ invertible. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies their integral full subcategories inside the derived category over the same completed coefficient sheaf, with the same reductions; in particular it supplies the required compatible etale-origin witnesses. Both rationalizations have the same objects and Hom groups tensored with $E$. The coefficient changes of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] are ordinary derived extension of completed coefficient rings. Those in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] are their completed versions, and [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies them by the canonical quotient-tower map. Hence the common-stage constructions agree with these specified comparisons, rather than merely sharing notation. The line from Step 2 is therefore an object of the stated category; its rationalization at stage $E$ is exactly the twist object of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

proof.text: Choose a common finite coefficient field for $K$ and the line, and let $C$ be the integral representative of $K$ there, justified by Step 3. Put $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $L=\mathcal O_E(m)_X$. The invertibility and integral membership assertions of [prop-weil-twist-preserves] give $L\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Since noetherian $X$ is quasi-compact and separated $X$ is quasi-separated, [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] applies to $C,L$: the ordinary product $C\otimes_B^L L$ is derived complete and its canonical quotient-tower comparison to $C\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}L$ is an isomorphism, natural in $C$. Step 2 identifies $L$ with the lisse realization of $\mathcal T_E$. Thus the ordinary twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and the completed tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] agree by this specified map. Rationalize and apply the common-stage tensor operation in that definition. Its scalar-extension comparisons and their tower compatibility, together with the coefficient compatibility of twisting supplied by [prop-weil-twist-preserves], make the resulting natural isomorphism independent of enlarging the field. This gives $K(m)\cong K\otimes^L\mathcal T$ and the asserted integral completeness. All integral tensors here are over $B$, never the discrete constant sheaf $(\mathcal O_E)_X$.
